concepts.title: Units of Digital Memory
concepts.definition: Stored data is counted in binary digits; eight of them form a byte, and bigger units such as kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte and terabyte are each 1024 times the unit just below them.
concepts.key_idea: Each step up the memory ladder multiplies the capacity by 1024, so conversions chain factor after factor.
question_patterns: Convert 4 GB into megabytes and then into kilobytes.
A pen drive is advertised as 64 GB. How many bytes can it hold?
How many bits are there in 2 MB of data?
Express a 700 MB movie file in kilobytes, taking 1024 as the multiplier at every step.
A laptop has 8 GB of RAM. Find its capacity in bytes.
Starting from bytes, write the full chain of conversions from 1 terabyte down to bits.

solution_steps.explain: Each gigabyte holds 1024 x 1024 x 1024 bytes.
One byte carries 8 bits, so multiply the byte total by 8.

worked_examples.q: A movie file occupies 4 GB of disk space. How many megabytes is that? (Take 1 GB = 1024 MB.)

concepts.title: Bits, Nibbles and Words
concepts.definition: A single binary digit is a bit; four bits grouped together make a nibble, two nibbles make a byte, and a word is the block of bits a processor handles in one go.
concepts.key_idea: Grouping starts at 4 bits per nibble and 8 bits per byte, then grows to the processor's word size.
question_patterns: How many nibbles are there in a 32-bit word?
A word measures 64 bits. How many bytes does it contain?
Give the number of bits in three nibbles and convert that into a byte count.
If a processor word is 16 bits wide, find how many nibbles and bytes it holds.
Why is an 8-bit word described as two nibbles? Show the counting.

solution_steps.explain: A nibble is 4 bits, so integer-divide the word width by 4.
A byte is 8 bits, so integer-divide the same width by 8.

worked_examples.q: A processor word is 64 bits wide. How many bytes does one word hold?

concepts.title: Data Transfer over the System Bus
concepts.definition: Wires that carry data, addresses and control signals between the CPU, memory and devices together form the system bus; moving a block of data takes at least its size divided by the link's transfer rate.
concepts.key_idea: The data bus runs both ways, while address and control buses carry information in one direction only.
question_patterns: How long does it take to move a 500 MB file across a link rated at 100 Mbps?
A hard disk sends a 1.5 GB backup over a 300 Mbps connection. Find the transfer time in seconds.
Why is the data bus bidirectional while the address bus is unidirectional?
Name the three buses that make up the system bus and state what each one carries.
Calculate the seconds needed to shift 250 MB of records across a 50 Mbps bus.
Which bus carries the memory location that the CPU wants to read, and in which direction?

solution_steps.explain: A rate in Mbps counts megabits, so multiply the megabyte size by 8.
Time in seconds equals megabits moved divided by megabits per second.

worked_examples.q: A 200 MB installer is fetched over a link rated at 100 Mbps. How many seconds does the transfer need? (1 MB = 8 megabits.)

concepts.title: Clock Speed and Instruction Throughput
concepts.definition: An internal clock emits pacing pulses at a fixed rate; a higher clock rate or fewer cycles needed per instruction lets the processor finish more instructions every second.
concepts.key_idea: A gigahertz rating means billions of pacing pulses each second, which sets the pace of execution.
question_patterns: A processor runs at 3 GHz and needs 2 cycles per instruction. How many instructions complete in one second?
Convert a 2.4 GHz clock into pulses per second.
Find the instructions-per-second figure for a 1 GHz chip taking 4 cycles per instruction.
How does the clock speed of a processor influence how fast programs run?
A chip executes 500 million instructions in half a second at 2 cycles per instruction. Estimate its clock rate in GHz.

solution_steps.action: turn the gigahertz clock into pulses per second
solution_steps.explain: One gigahertz is a billion pulses per second, so multiply by 10 to the power 9.

solution_steps.action: divide by cycles needed per instruction
solution_steps.explain: Instructions finished per second equals the pulse rate split by the cycles each instruction consumes.

worked_examples.q: A CPU clock paces at 2 GHz and each instruction needs 4 cycles. How many million instructions finish per second?

concepts.title: Moore's Law Transistor Growth
concepts.definition: An observation made in 1965 that the count of transistors fitted onto a single chip tends to double roughly every two years, which drives the exponential rise in computing power.
concepts.key_idea: A count that doubles every two years turns modest beginnings into astronomically dense chips within a decade.
question_patterns: A 1971 chip carried 2300 transistors. Using the doubling-every-two-years rule, estimate the count ten years later.
If a chip holds 100 million transistors today, how many doublings pass in 8 years and what count follows?
State what Moore's Law predicts about transistor counts on a microchip.
A microchip had 4000 transistors in 2000. Project the figure for 2008 using the two-year doubling rule.
How many two-year doubling periods fit into 14 years, and by what factor does the count grow?

solution_steps.explain: One period is two years, so integer-divide the elapsed years by 2.
Each period doubles the count, so multiply the starting figure by 2 raised to the number of periods.

worked_examples.q: A chip carries 4000 transistors today. If the count doubles every 2 years, how many transistors will it carry after 6 years?

concepts.title: Structured, Semi-structured and Unstructured Data
concepts.definition: Records that sit in fixed rows and columns are structured; items carrying internal tags, like HTML pages or CSV files, are semi-structured; free-form media such as audio, video and photographs are unstructured.
concepts.formula: classify(source) as structured, semi-structured or unstructured
concepts.key_idea: Check for a rigid table format, internal tags, or neither, and that decides the data type.
question_patterns: Categorise an HTML page, a railway booking record and a satellite image as structured, semi-structured or unstructured.
Give two everyday examples of unstructured data and justify your choice.
A school keeps attendance in a table of roll number, name, month and percentage. Which data type is this?
What marks semi-structured data apart from unstructured data?
Sort these into the three data types: cricket score sheet, MP3 song, email document.
Why can a CSV file be called semi-structured even though it lacks a fixed schema?

solution_steps.explain: A strict row-and-column format signals structured data; tags or markers inside the item signal semi-structured data; neither sign means unstructured data.

worked_examples.q: A marksheet table has fixed rows and columns. Is it structured, semi-structured or unstructured data?

concepts.title: Language Translators and Machine Code
concepts.definition: A processor acts only on machine code, so source code must first be converted: assemblers handle assembly language, compilers render a whole program in one pass, and interpreters convert plus run a single line at a time.
concepts.key_idea: A compiled program runs afterwards without its translator, but an interpreted program needs the interpreter present on every run.
question_patterns: How does a computer make sense of a program typed in a high level language?
Distinguish a compiler from an interpreter and give one advantage of each.
Why does machine code usually finish running sooner than its source code?
What is the job of an assembler, and which language does it accept?
Name the three kinds of translators used in a computing system.
Python code is executed line by line. Which translator style does this show, and why?

solution_steps.action: match the language to its translator
solution_steps.explain: Assembly language maps to an assembler; a high level language maps to a compiler (whole program at once) or an interpreter (one line at a time), and the output that the CPU runs is machine code.

worked_examples.q: Which translator converts a whole high-level program into machine code in one pass?

worked_examples.title: Size of a 2 GB video in bits
worked_examples.problem: A movie file occupies 2 GB of disk space. Express its size first in megabytes and then in bits.

steps.explain: Each megabyte is 1024 kilobytes, each kilobyte 1024 bytes, and each byte 8 bits.

worked_examples.answer_note: The clip measures 2048 MB, which is 17179869184 bits of storage.

worked_examples.title: Download time for a 500 MB installer at 100 Mbps
worked_examples.problem: An installer of 500 MB is fetched over a connection rated at 100 Mbps. How many seconds does the download need?

steps.explain: A rate in Mbps counts megabits, so multiply megabytes by 8.
Seconds equal megabits split by megabits per second.

worked_examples.answer_note: The transfer carries 4000 megabits, so it needs 40 seconds.

Convert 3 GB of data into bytes and then into bits.
A 2 GB backup moves across a 200 Mbps link. Work out the transfer time in seconds.
